a: Multiple streams share one TCP connection, reducing connection overhead.
HTTP/3 runs on QUIC/UDP for faster connection setup and less head-of-line blocking.
TLS negotiates keys and authenticates the server (and optionally the client).
CT logs public certificates to detect mis-issuance.
HSTS forces HTTPS; preload lists harden first-visit protection.
A cache hit serves from the edge without contacting origin.
An intermediate cache layer reduces stampedes to origin.
Brotli/gzip compress text responses to save bandwidth.
ETags enable conditional requests that return 304 when unchanged.
Vary tells shared caches which request headers change the response.
